name: Joy Ericson
headline: Celebrating Joy Ericson
summary: A member since 1967, a certified flower show judge for more than 40 years, and a past president who still mentors fellow members in the art of floral arrangement.

portrait.alt: Joy Ericson standing in front of a wall of framed floral entries, wearing her judge's badge at the Philadelphia Flower Show.
portrait.caption: Joy at the Philadelphia Flower Show

secondary.alt: Joy Ericson smiling at a lunch table beneath a canopy of tropical plants.

chapters.label: The Beginning
chapters.text: In 1967, Joy was invited to join the Garden Gate Garden Club (GGGC) by a fellow mom on her street. Her first flower show competition was a team effort with that same friend. Their floral arrangement, inspired by Andrew Wyeth, earned second place and sparked Joy’s competitive nature and passion for flower shows.

chapters.label: Becoming a Judge
chapters.text: In the early 1980s, the Delaware Federation of Garden Clubs offered classes in Flower Show Judging. Joy enrolled and became a certified flower show judge, a role she has held for more than 40 years!

chapters.label: On the World Stage
chapters.text: Today, Joy is a highly respected international judge, having judged flower shows throughout the United States and at international events as far south as Peru. Earlier this year, she judged her 40th Philadelphia Flower Show, the oldest and largest flower show in the United States.

chapters.label: Giving Back
chapters.text: Joy has also served as President of the GGGC and continues to be a valued mentor to fellow members, sharing her expertise in the art of floral arrangement and presentation.

stats.label: Years as a certified flower show judge

note.text: Joy’s name also lives on in the club’s CEW Training Award.
